definitions.explanation: A soft covering of cloth that wraps the head, sometimes also the neck and shoulders. In Japan schoolchildren keep a padded {防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん} at their desks to protect the head in an earthquake.

examples.japanese: {頭巾|ずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧。
⟦{避難訓練|ひなんくんれん}→避難訓練：28230_hinankunren⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶった→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧。
examples.english: We put on our disaster hoods during the evacuation drill.

examples.japanese: ⟦{赤|あか}い→赤い：00585_akai⟧{頭巾|ずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶった→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧⟦{女|おんな}の{子|こ}→女の子：02865_onnanoko⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{森|もり}→森：02260_mori⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{中|なか}→中：00654_naka⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{歩|ある}いて→歩く：00538_aruku⟧いく。
examples.english: A girl in a red hood walks through the forest.

notes:
The usual verb is ⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧, as for a hat. A hood attached to a coat or sweatshirt is ⟦フード→フード：28535_fuudo⟧; {頭巾|ずきん} is a separate piece of cloth.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {頭巾|ずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かぶる→かぶる：00709_kaburu⟧: to put on a hood
- {防災頭巾|ぼうさいずきん}: padded disaster hood (kept at schools)
- ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧ずきん: Little Red Riding Hood
- {頭巾|ずきん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧とる: to take off a hood
